newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen rebounding.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen rebounding.

text.p: Polish shares fell for a third consecutive session, pulled lower by profit-taking after recent 2.7-percent growth and by a busy primary market, but analysts expected a rebound in the next few sessions.

The main market's WIG index fell 173.8 points or 1.1 percent, to 15,818.3, and turnover fell five percent to 132 million zlotys ($41.3 million) on all three markets as 72 issues fell, 19 rose and 13 were flat.

Analysts said the upside was limited as the primary market was drawing investor capital and attention to offers such as that of Bank Handlowy, in which one billion zlotys ($312 million) worth shares are on sale, and copper giant KGHM expected later in June.
"The market is reacting according to the pattern that... demand appears after falls, so the market is starting to rebound," said Grzegorz Cimochowski, an analyst of ING Barings.
Buying was stronger after the price fixing and most stocks closed higher in continuous trade than their fixing levels.
But analysts were divided over whether the market's rebound would happen on Friday, when Bank Handlowy ends its first and most attractive subscription period for individual investors.
Analysts said that in the longer-term the market might keep its sideways drift until elections, expected in September.
Some said, however, that more privatisations and new issues might contribute to falls on the exchange in June.
